clue.text: Rock band's also touring large part of Australia

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the band and the word for also travel round the L

parts.note: Queen is the British rock band, and the 's supplies an S
also means and
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A famous rock group is also on a tour of a big chunk of Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' wraps the band and AND around L. Queen is the British rock group fronted by Freddie Mercury.
explanation.definitionFit: The state in the north-east of Australia covers a vast area, so it is fairly called a large part of the country.

clue.text: Worthless article yields nothing for American

indicators.note: yields means gives way, so one letter surrenders its place to another
for here means in exchange for, so the new letter takes the old one's place

parts.note: an article is an object, a thing
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An item of no value gives up nothing to an American buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yields' and 'for' tell you the O of OBJECT gives way to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes something wretched and contemptible, of no worth or dignity.

clue.text: Expel from university without reason extremely shocked individual

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so those two letters sit around the next piece
extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of the word shocked

parts.note: an end is a purpose or reason, as in 'to that end'
own means particular to an individual, as in 'a room of one's own'

explanation.surface: A student is thrown out of college for no reason, leaving one person deeply shocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside; 'extremely' takes the outer letters of shocked.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities, to send someone down is to expel or rusticate a student.

clue.text: Second European defends abuse over guitarist originally in Blur

indicators.note: defends means protects by surrounding, so the outer pair encloses the rest
in a down clue over means above, so the first piece sits before the second

parts.note: mud is abuse or slander, as in 'mud-slinging'

indicators.note: originally means at the beginning, so take the first letter of guitarist

explanation.surface: A second European protects a musician from insults over the original guitarist of the band Blur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defends' puts MUD plus G between S and E. Blur is a 1990s British band, here the definition in its plain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge is a blurred smear, and to smudge is to make indistinct.

clue.text: Campaigns running scared, limiting empty undertakings

indicators.note: limiting means bounding on both sides, so the rearranged letters enclose the other piece
running in the sense of moving about, so the letters of scared are rearranged
empty means hollowed out, keeping only the outside letters of undertakings

explanation.surface: Nervous campaigners run, restricting pointless ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges the letters of scared as CRADES, and 'limiting' puts the hollowed undertakings inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusades are vigorous campaigns for a cause, from the medieval holy wars.

clue.text: Antipodean principal, small of stature reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: key means principal, as in a key figure, and wee is Scottish for small; together they are said as one word

explanation.surface: A head teacher from down under is said to be rather short.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiwi is the informal name for a New Zealander, someone from the Antipodes.

clue.text: Last piece of Arctic roll for dessert

indicators.note: the last piece of a word is its final letter, here of Arctic

parts.note: a roll of thunder is a rumble

explanation.surface: The final slice of an Arctic roll is served for pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Arctic roll is a British frozen dessert of sponge wrapped around ice cream, which makes 'roll' look part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumble is a baked pudding of fruit under a crumbly topping.

clue.text: Film excerpt about reptile, current connection with it?

indicators.note: about means concerning, so the clip is about the reptile and the reptile is named first

parts.note: a crocodile is a large reptile
a clip is a short excerpt from a film

explanation.surface: A nature-film extract about a crocodile, and an electrical connector named after one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' and the question mark hint that the connector has the reptile in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile clip is a spring-loaded toothed clamp used to make a temporary electrical connection.

clue.text: Military order read out

indicators.note: read out says the word is spoken, so a word sounding like it is entered

parts.note: to marshal is to arrange or put in order

explanation.surface: An army command is announced aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial describes things to do with war and soldiers, as in martial law.

clue.text: Inclined to steal gin, the girl fed appallingly

indicators.note: appallingly means dreadfully, signalling these letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl who was fed gin dreadfully might be tempted to pilfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-fingered is the idiom for someone prone to petty theft.

clue.text: Somehow depend on keeping agreement essentially indeterminate

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the rearranged letters enclose the middle letter
somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of depend on are rearranged
essentially points to the essence or centre, the middle letter of agreement

explanation.surface: An undecided agreement somehow depends on a central point.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal at the start rearranges DEPEND ON as OPENNDED; 'essentially' gives E, the middle of agreement; 'keeping' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-ended has no fixed limit or conclusion, so it is indefinite.

clue.text: Smart chain mayor finally removed

indicators.note: removed says that letter is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: a string, as of pearls or shops, is a chain

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of mayor

explanation.surface: A chain of office is taken from the mayor, which stings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R, which 'removed' takes out of STRING.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart and to sting both mean to feel a sharp pain.

clue.text: Start working with firm

parts.note: on means working or operating, as in 'the machine is on'
set means firm or solid, as in 'the jelly is set'

explanation.surface: Begin a job with a company.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning, as in the onset of winter.

clue.text: Finished plan creating bank facility for customers

parts.note: over means finished, as in 'the game is over'
a draft is a preliminary plan or outline

explanation.surface: A completed scheme sets up a new banking service for clients.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft lets a bank's customers spend beyond their balance, an arranged lending facility.

clue.text: Newscasters in US on CNN are changing

indicators.note: changing means altering, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Television presenters at the American network CNN are being replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Announcers are broadcasters who read news and introduce programmes.

clue.text: Arrest adult trio that's regularly expressed upsetting language

indicators.note: upsetting means turning over, so the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to catch or arrest them
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: regularly expressed means only every other letter of trio is given voice

explanation.surface: Three grown-ups are arrested for repeatedly using offensive words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly expressed' takes T and I from trio; 'upsetting' reverses NAILATI.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is the Romance tongue spoken in Italy.

clue.text: Current lawsuit leads to state where nothing's happening

parts.note: in means current or fashionable, as in 'what's in this season'
an action is a lawsuit, a case brought in court

explanation.surface: A present legal case results in a standstill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like electricity (I), but it is IN, fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a lack of activity, a situation in which nothing is done.

clue.text: Hound immoral head of judiciary in Northern Ireland

parts.note: base means low or immoral, as in 'base motives'

indicators.note: in says that letter is placed inside the abbreviation
head of means the first letter of judiciary

explanation.surface: Pursue a corrupt senior judge in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a verb to harass, but it is the noun: a breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a barkless African hunting dog, a breed of hound.

clue.text: Person withdrawing library books, one with 13 perhaps?

definitions.meaning: someone who takes books out of a library on loan
13-across is a bank facility; anyone who has one owes the bank money

explanation.walkthrough: 13 refers to the answer at 13-across, OVERDRAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Library users take out books on loan, and anyone overdrawn owes money to the bank.

clue.text: Go crazy around Eve

indicators.note: crazy means wild or mad, so the letters of around and Eve are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Eve's partner goes mad running rings round her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like an instruction to put something round Eve, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is to make an attempt or effort, which is an endeavour.

clue.text: Competed in medieval combat re-enactment topless, getting thrown out!

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, which in a down answer is the first letter

parts.note: knights jousted on horseback with lances, a combat often re-enacted today

explanation.surface: A knight in a mock tournament loses his helmet and gets knocked off his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousted means expelled or removed from a position.

clue.text: Cast finishes off brief rehearsal you began watching

indicators.note: finishes off means the last letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The actors finish a short run-through that you started watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors, but it is a verb in the past: thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast and the answer both mean thrown, as a dice or a net is thrown.

clue.text: Rearing cheetahs, it effectively inspires obsession

indicators.note: Rearing says the hidden letters are read backwards
inspires, read as breathes life into, says the answer lies within the preceding words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Breeding cheetahs well becomes a consuming passion.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft defined with 'inspires obsession', a verb phrase that cannot stand for a noun; 'inspires' instead signals the hidden letters. In a down answer 'Rearing' means rising, so they read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an object of fixation, something given an irrational devotion.

clue.text: Unknown cuts record for composer

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a list is a written record of items
Z is one of the algebraic letters for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: An anonymous person edits a recording for a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic composer and pianist.

clue.text: Son given powerful injection

parts.note: hot can mean strong or potent, as in a hot curry

explanation.surface: A boy is given a strong jab.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is informal for a jab or hypodermic dose, as in a flu shot.

clue.text: Wager Mark will find something fast to drive?

parts.note: to sport is an old sense meaning to stake or wager money
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: Bet that Mark will find a speedy vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it is a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports car is a fast, low performance automobile built for driving pleasure.

clue.text: Suggest what experienced fashion model might exhibit?

parts.note: a pro is a professional, someone experienced
models strike a pose for the camera

explanation.surface: What stance would a seasoned catwalk model display?
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to put forward an idea for consideration.

clue.text: Unfortunately rudeness almost is guaranteed

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the remaining letters are rearranged
almost means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Sadly, rudeness is assured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last S of rudeness; 'Unfortunately' rearranges RUDENES.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ensured something is to have made it certain, so it is assured.
